title: supervisor MCP timed out twice (-32001); CLI fallback used
body: supervisor__verdict and supervisor__fanout_search MCP calls returned error -32001 Request timed out at session start; per AGENTS.md fallback rule the CLI tools (session_start.py unified verdict, engram_supervise.py) were used instead and delivered CLARIFY consistently. MCP server works for plan_items/triage_plan/task_detail, so the timeout is load/latency-bound, not a dead server.

title: git at C:/Azazael root fails - repo root is C:/Azazael/azazael
body: Ran git log from C:/Azazael (the Freebuff session project root) and got fatal: not a git repository. The project root contains TWO nested repos (azazael/.git, azazael-coord/.git); every git command must cd into one of them. Discovered via ls -d */.git probe after the failure.

title: Inline python -c with nested quoting raised SyntaxError; heredoc script file works
body: An inline python -c used for the azazael-coord scan broke on backslash/path quoting and raised SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character. Re-ran as a heredoc-written /tmp script invoked via cygpath -w. Same failure class as the recorded over-scripting lesson: keep analysis code in script files, not shell-quoted one-liners.

title: grep -c on unreadable files yields empty; bash [ -gt ] spews integer expression errors
body: Shell loop tested [ "$n" -gt 0 ] where n came from grep -c that output nothing for unreadable/binary files, producing ~400 'integer expression expected' stderr lines and silently skipping those files. Guard with [ -n "$n" ] or do counting in Python. The errors were noise, but the silent skip hid real candidates until a Python rescan.

title: FALSIFIED own finding: DEAD-AT-HEAD was actually alive-untracked
body: First forensic pass declared state/BRIEF_884_MIMO_MERGE.md and state/MIMO_STRAIGHTEN_REPORT dead because git cat-file -e HEAD: failed. Both exist in the worktree as UNTRACKED files (git-invisible). Corrected with a full-depth find before reporting. Git-tracked absence is not filesystem absence; checks must cover both planes.

title: Read-only audit baseline saved as a COUNT not a list - delta unattributable
body: Saved git status --porcelain | wc -l (12) before the sweep; later the count was 13 with no repo writes issued by any command (all outputs to %TEMP% and /tmp). Because only the count was instrumented, the changed entry cannot be attributed - suspected concurrent lane or daemon. Save the full entry list as the baseline in future read-only passes.

title: Env-drift probe checked root/docs/state only - absences are not proofs of absence
body: The environment drift probe searched root, docs and state in each local env (find -maxdepth 3 in WSL), so subdir copies (skills/, research/, output/) were undercounted - RESEARCH_RECORD.md and EVE_UNLEASHED_TODO.md appeared missing from windows until a full find located them. Table absences were reported with an explicit scope caveat instead of as negatives.

title: G: archive manifest grep required format check before claiming file absence
body: Before declaring 2 task files absent from the 5080-file archive, read MANIFEST.jsonl row format ({tier,src,dst,bytes,sha256,verified}) and confirmed the name-based grep covers the stored paths; broad keyword grep also returned 0. Verification rule 4 applied: read the cited line before accepting the instrument's finding.

title: Bulk gate blocked the 3961-line deletion commit; sanctioned ALLOW_BULK_COMMIT=1 used
body: Pre-commit bulk gate rejected the NEURAL_MESH_FUNCTION_TODO.md deletion (3961 lines vs 150/file cap). Analyzed before re-running: a deletion cannot be split, and the gate's own contract offers ALLOW_BULK_COMMIT=1 as a declaration to justify in the commit message. Re-ran with the flag and full in-message justification; all six gates then green (scanner, canon, ratchet, mesh, paradigm, supervisor).

title: FALSIFIED own class: checkbox-regex counts vs status-marker counts are incommensurable
body: The forensic class 'CONSUMED-BUT-OPEN (zero checkboxes vs claimed counts)' collapsed under line-level re-verification: minted counts used BLOCKED/stale/todo status-marker rows while the sweep counted only dash-bracket checkboxes. The live files still carry their rows (T-n table, 23 status rows). Reversed the class BEFORE any disposition destroyed live task state; recorded supersedes judgment against the earlier observation.

title: Pipeline rc trap reprised three times: cmd | head; echo $? reports head's status
body: artifact_freshness rc, git grep rc and earlier grep rc were all read after a pipe, so the printed rc was head's exit code, not the instrument's. rc-carrying commands must write rc before any pipe or run unpiped. This is the same class as the recorded heredoc-pipe lint motivation; caught by re-reading each command line, not by a gate.

title: #1238 'mislocation' was a search-key artifact; item was accurate as minted
body: The plan item already named desktop/EveUnleashed_Selector/docs/POSTDOC_RESEARCH_MANIFEST.md in its Where field; only the supervisor display truncated the path to the basename, which sent the forensic search to repo root. Read the item text before correcting the item - the fix belongs to the search key, not the record.

title: SOP.md canon drift root cause: canon doc absent from SYNC_DOC_PATTERNS
body: G: source-of-truth carried a stale SOP.md with a duplicate 6-box checklist because sync_all.py never synced SOP.md - it was missing from SYNC_DOC_PATTERNS. Added it, verified membership by dry-run list inspection (count alone would not have proven it). MANDATES.md has the identical gap and is filed as a plan goal.

title: pmb__update_goal rejected progress 4x: schema wants a JSON number, string 100 fails every attempt
body: Four consecutive pmb__update_goal calls failed with the same zod union error (expected number, received string) on the progress parameter. It must be emitted as a bare JSON number (100), not a quoted string. Omitting progress entirely is the fallback: status alone still closes the goal and the tool then reports progress 100 itself. Repeated retries with identical payloads are wasted turns - inspect the schema error shape once, then change the payload TYPE, not the value.

title: str_replace oldString mismatch on sync_all.py: edited from remembered comment text instead of re-read content
body: The MANDATES.md pattern edit failed because oldString carried comment text as remembered from the earlier SOP.md edit, not as the file actually held it. Protocol rule 4 (read the cited line before accepting) applies to EDIT targets too: code_search the anchor, windowed-read the exact region, write oldString from the read output, never from memory of what was written earlier.

title: gitignore state/* contradicted the durable-record claim; 30-file tracked precedent resolved the force-add question
body: Committing the forensic report failed: .gitignore:257 state/* ignores state/, so the record cited as durable by Engram #1316/#1317 was untracked and would not survive. Resolution: git ls-files state/ showed 30 tracked state files, establishing force-add precedent; committed with -f and justification in-message (fa026dc9). A record is not durable until a tracked ref holds it; re-check ignore status with git check-ignore -v at the moment of the add, since ignore state can change mid-session.

title: Near-miss avoided: mesh trio regeneration would have clobbered a concurrent lane's uncommitted WIRE_OR_CUT.json edit
body: The stale-artifact goal said refresh the worklist via refresh_all, but the only clearable row (WORKLIST 150 sources newer) is regenerated by a trio that REWRITES NEURAL_MESH_WIRE_OR_CUT.json - which git status shows modified in-worktree by a concurrent lane. Running it would overwrite their uncommitted work. Deferred with evidence recorded instead. Before any regeneration step, git status the OUTPUT files it writes, not just the inputs it reads - concurrent-lane clobber is invisible from the staleness audit alone.

title: sick :8080 premise falsified by health probe; destructive restart/retire avoided on a live traffic-serving server
body: The sidecars goal read restart-or-retire a sick mxba :8080 server. netstat showed PID 20932 listening with live TIME_WAIT traffic and /health returned HTTP 200 serving mxbai-embed-large. The premise was 2 days stale. Killing or restarting would have disrupted live inference traffic for no defect. Resolution was evidence, not action: goal closed as premise-falsified. Destructive verbs in a goal title do not authorize the destructive branch when verification shows no defect exists.

title: Bake-lane append repeated the W1-02 failure class in the same session: anchor written from memory, not from the file tail
body: The first attempt to append these rows anchored oldString on an earlier row remembered from conversation summary; the file's actual last line was FFI-13. The fix pattern (read the exact region first) had been written to this very lane minutes earlier and was still violated once. Self-referential error: a lesson recorded is not a lesson applied. Anchor appends on tail -c output, not on recall.

title: Refusal ledger writes duplicate rows for one refusal event
body: Audit of state/supervisor_refusals.jsonl (241 rows) found 5 groups of byte-identical (ts, client, tool, detail) entries totalling 7 extra rows, e.g. x4 at 2026-10-19T00:35:32.641Z for 'conflicts: 33 unresolved'. The ledger is the evidence base for refusal frequency, so ~3% inflation makes every refusal statistic soft. OPEN - not previously logged.

title: Error taxonomy: claim, reading and closure fail by one defect at three altitudes
body: Fanned-out review of ERROR_LOG (164 entries to #218), 2026-10-18 lanes, prior transcript gate output and memory lessons. Classes A (claim exceeds evidence), B (instrument misread: truncation, pipeline rc, literal grep, 0-item collect, wrong interpreter) and C (DONE closures from a scanner summary) are the same failure: stopping at the first confirming instrument. RULE 0B-E was written from this defect and it recurred 4+ documented times after codification.

title: AP-5 gate scope: opencode.db only, so this client's own prose is unauditable
body: transcript_ap5_gate.py scanned 63 assistant parts across 1 session in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db and reported 2 want_me_to findings. Freebuff session output is not in that store, so AP-5 compliance for freebuff cannot be evidenced with the current gate. Recorded as a coverage limit, never as a pass.

title: Stale refusal timestamp is not a live condition: 0 pending conflicts reproduced
body: The refusal ledger's newest rows (2026-10-19T03:00:40/53Z) cite 3 unresolved conflicts, while engram conflicts stats now reports 0 pending (deferred 0, dead 0). Re-derived rather than repeating the ledger's number - the 03:00 refusals are historical, not an open blocker.

title: Self-correction: ER-01 was reported as novel; the duplicate-row class was codified 2026-10-09
body: Memory query (PMB 001a1216e880e, Engram #340) shows the duplicate-rows-inflate-a-count arithmetic was already codified three days before ER-01 called it 'not previously logged'. Only the INSTANCE (state/supervisor_refusals.jsonl) is new; the CLASS is prior art. ER-01's novelty claim retracted; artifact corrected in place. Recorded because a review that audits overclaim must not commit one.

title: Four pending goals are already satisfied at HEAD — close, do not assign workers
body: Verified against source, not the task text: (1) tools/test_paradigm_gate.py IS wired into .githooks/pre-commit as blocking check 7b; (2) claim_guard.py IS invoked by .githooks/prepare-commit-msg ('unwired' is stale for the commit path only); (3) GGUFAnalyzer.find_quantizer :388, _run_quantizer :392 and convert :395 all exist in ORCHESTRATION/ml_platforms/universal_converter.py; (4) tests/test_store_guard.py exists with 4 pinned tests covering local_memory and direct_memory default-path refusal. Each would otherwise have consumed a worker.

title: Duplicate goal filings would double-assign the same work
body: Two independent pairs name the same job: the git-bash vs Python /tmp divergence is filed twice (001a13b61d30e and 001a12c9be653), and Wave 3 trainer retirement is filed twice (001a1416b80d8 and 001a12c318f88). Fan-out assigns by file, so a duplicate id is how two workers end up editing the same target. Dedupe is a precondition of the batch plan, not a cleanup task.

title: Encoding slice manifest premise unverified: no S031-S043 artifact exists
body: Engram #984/#956/#999/#1006 describe 13 remaining slices, 52 files, 87 sites at S031-S043. A grep for a slice manifest or S031/S043 identifiers returned 0 matches, so the premise is not reproducible from the tree. It must be re-derived before ANY worker is assigned an encoding slice - handing 13 workers a manifest nobody can find is the same defect class as the falsified DONE closures.

title: Worker capability bounds the slice shape: no terminal means coordinator owns verification
body: The fan-out workers read and edit files but cannot execute. Every slice must therefore be writable without running it, and the coordinator owns the test/typecheck half. A plan that says 'worker runs the gate' is unexecutable by construction - same shape as the exercise-only measurements the wire-or-cut ledger exists to catch.

title: Test helper passed a generator to len(), so the wiring tests had never run
body: tests/test_preflight_gate_wiring.py called len(_non_comment_lines(text)) where the helper is a generator: TypeError on first execution. The crashed session wrote the tests and never ran them, so a green-looking artifact was in fact unrunnable. Fixed by counting the generator explicitly.

title: An existence guard was credited as a gate invocation
body: The matcher counted `if [ -f tools/preflight_all.py ]` as an execution, so the hook could lose the real invocation and still pass. Existence tests are now excluded, and a negative control asserts a guard-only stanza yields no invoked scripts.

title: Hook-parity detector matched only lower-case python, missing the pinned $PYTHON3
body: preflight_all.hook_gate_scripts tested `"python" in line`, so every $PYTHON3 invocation was invisible: scripts/commit_gate.py was reported registered-but-not-run while the hook runs it on line 44. Matching is now case-insensitive and accepts PMB_PY.

title: An echo remediation hint was counted as gate execution
body: The supervisor stanza prints 'then: python tools/supervisor_doctor.py --fix'. Parity counted that echo as a run and reported supervisor_doctor as ran-but-unregistered. Echo lines are now skipped, the same rule the hook-wiring matcher already used.

title: Interpreter NAME resolved to WindowsApps 3.13.14, which cannot import mcp
body: preflight ran the supervisor gate through resolve_interpreter('python3'), which is PATH python3 (3.13.14) and failed in 0.16s with ModuleNotFoundError while the same command passed under 3.15t. python3/py315t now resolve to the pinned venv. A resolved name is not a running interpreter.

title: Ollama discovery offered embedding-only models for generation
body: discover_all published every /api/tags entry as a generation model, so run_inference fell back to available_models[0] = nomic-embed-text:latest, which answers /api/generate with HTTP 400. Filtering now uses the capabilities the server reports, with the name-prefix list as fallback.

title: The Eve model combo was cosmetic: selected Ollama model was dropped
body: _run_inference honoured selected_model_path only for C:\ GGUF paths, so selecting eve-v2u changed nothing and the run used the backend default. An e2e that only checked 'a response arrived' would pass without Eve driving it. The override is now passed to run_inference(model=...).

title: Kilo's discovery test asserted a recorded count (>=8 models) that had gone stale
body: tests/test_model_discovery.py required >= 8 Ollama models, a number recorded 2026-08-27 when the host held 14; the server now advertises 4, so two tests failed. Replaced with equality against the live /api/tags list and a generation-capability check; GGUF assertions now require existing files rather than a count.

title: Four engine tests swallowed every exception and could not fail for the reason they named
body: test_eve_engine.py wrapped expected failures in try/except/pass, so a KeyError or ValueError raised anywhere (or nothing raised at all) passed. Replaced with pytest.raises for the two error paths and a result assertion for infer_async.

title: A glyph-parsing tool tripped the unicode_emoji rule it exists to parse
body: closure_basis_check.py carried literal status glyphs in docstrings and one runtime rule string, adding 3 unicode_emoji findings. The vocabularies are now written as code points (U+2B1C etc.) and matched by code point, so behaviour is identical without emoji in source.
